title: 15th Sitting of Second session of 2026
summary: The sitting opened at 09:01 and closed at 10:23. Members continued debating a resolution by the Kendhoo member, Mauroof Zakir, on state companies cutting staff, which he says is happening for political reasons. Opposition members backed it, while government-side members said dismissals follow company rules and pointed to dismissals under the previous government. The debate ended with members still waiting to speak and no vote. The house then approved the Economic Committee's pick of Fathimath Ameeza as Commissioner General of Taxation, 64 votes to none.

items.title: Opening of the sitting and prayers
items.outcome: sitting opened by the Speaker at 09:01

items.title: Attendance of members at the sitting
Resolution by the Kendhoo member on state companies reducing staff and politically motivated dismissals
items.outcome: debated; debate closed with speakers still waiting, no vote recorded in this part

items.title: Economic Committee report on the President's nominees for Commissioner General of Taxation (Tax Administration Act 3/2010, art. 8(a))
items.outcome: debated by two parties; sent to a vote

items.title: Vote on appointing Fathimath Ameeza as Commissioner General of Taxation

speakers.name: Mauroof Zakir
positions: Said the government treats workers as commodities and dismisses them for political reasons; objected to labour rights being placed under Home Security.
Urged company workers to form unions and use the right to protest.

speakers.name: Saudulla Hilmy
positions: Said dismissals are the employer's responsibility and follow company rules; recalled staff cuts under the earlier government.
As Economic Committee deputy chair, presented the report on the Commissioner General of Taxation nominees.

speakers.name: Dr. Ahmed Shamheed
positions: Backed the resolution, saying state-company staff are being dismissed for opposition links while company losses and debts grow and no clear procedure exists.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Didi
positions: Raised a point of order that labour matters sit with the Ministry of Labour, not Home Security.

speakers.name: Mohamed Ismail
positions: Raised a point of order that the President did not make the statement attributed to him in the debate.

speakers.name: Ahmed Saleem
positions: Said some staff cuts are unavoidable given war-related costs to the state budget, and the government's steps are reasonable; corruption can only be reduced gradually.

speakers.name: Ali Moosa
positions: Opposed the resolution as politically driven, recalled dismissals under the previous MDP government, and cited government job and scholarship programmes.

speakers.name: Abdul Rahman
positions: Did not support the resolution, calling it party-driven, but also opposed politically motivated dismissals and called for merit-based hiring.

speakers.name: Mohamed Fazeel
positions: Opposed the resolution, said this government does not dismiss for politics, and listed dismissals of civil servants, security staff and judges under the MDP.

speakers.name: Mohamed Musthafa Ibrahim
positions: Said the resolution itself accepts job cuts are needed, that it cites no specific case of political dismissal, and opposed it.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Hussain
positions: Compared public job numbers at the end of the MDP and earlier governments, said dismissals follow rules, and called for growing the private sector.

speakers.name: Ahmed Aifan
positions: Opposed the resolution, saying claims of political dismissals are false, and pointed to staff placed in company management by the earlier government.

speakers.name: Ameen Faisal
positions: Supported the resolution and cited the President's pledge that nobody loses a job over political views; said dismissals need a proper procedure.

speakers.name: Husnee Mubarik
positions: Called the resolution baseless, said no one in his constituency was dismissed politically, and cited past transfers of staff between islands.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Nazil
positions: Supported the Economic Committee report and said both nominees are qualified for the post, as the committee interviews showed.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Falah
positions: Supported the report, citing committee scores of 92.44% for Fathimath Ameeza and 82.89% for Mohamed Haleem, and her long service at the tax authority.

decisions: Fathimath Ameeza (G.Dh. Gaddoo) was approved as Commissioner General of Taxation by 64 votes to none.
Debate on the Economic Committee report was closed and a full-house committee was announced for 11:00.

votes.what: Appointment of Fathimath Ameeza as Commissioner General of Taxation (93 members in total, 65 present, 33 needed to pass)
